BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

    IN THE MATTER OF SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC                        )
    SERVICE COMPANY’S APPLICATION FOR: (1)                      )
    REVISION OF ITS RETAIL RATES UNDER                          )    Docket No. 25-00079-UT
    ADVICE NOTICE 341; AND (2) OTHER                            )
    ASSOCIATED RELIEF                                           )


    ORDER GRANTING LEAVE TO FILE RESPONSES TO EXCEPTIONS AND ORDER
       REQUIRING RESPONSE TO STAFF’S MOTION FOR ORAL ARGUMENT
           THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission upon

Southwestern Public Service Company’s (“SPS”) Expedited Motion for Leave to File Limited

Response to Staff’s Exceptions to Certification of Stipulation (“Motion to Respond”) and the

Commission’s Utility Division Staff’s (“Staff”) Motion for Oral Argument.

                                                 BACKGROUND

           1.       On November 2, 2026, Staff, SPS, and other Signatories to the Stipulation in the

proceeding filed exceptions to the Certification of Stipulation filed in this docket.

           2.       In Staff’s Exceptions, Staff requested that the Commission decline to adopt the

Certification of Stipulation’s recommendation to approve Section 1.1 of the Stipulation, which

addresses SPS’s proposed Base Rate Increase, arguing that SPS has not carried its burden to prove

that Section 1.1 would result in fair, just, and reasonable rates. 1 As an alternative to the denial,

Staff suggests that the Commission conditionally approve the filing subject to SPS submitting

 undated financial load forecasts, resource-adequacy information, actual linkage date, and related

reconciliations before compliance tariffs take effect.2

          3.     On November 4, 2026, SPS filed its Motion asking for leave to respond to the

alternative-compliance filing proposal in Staff’s Exceptions.

          4.     On November 4, 2026, Staff filed a Motion for Oral Argument seeking to offer oral

argument on the following issue:

          “Has Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”) fulfilled its burden of proof that the

          Contested Stipulation results in fair, just, and reasonable rates and is in accordance with

          law where:

                  A. the revenue requirement is based upon stale linkage data?

                 B. the jurisdictional allocation between Texas and New Mexico has not been

                 adjusted for differences in test periods between the two states and will cause

                 overcollection of the jurisdictional allocation of the revenue requirement

                 from New Mexico customers?”

                                FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS
          5.     The Commission’s procedural rules do not provide for responses to Exceptions to

Certification of Stipulations, unless otherwise stated by the Commission.3 Nevertheless, Staff’s

Exceptions include a proposed alternative remedy involving additional compliance filings. The

 Commission finds that permitting a response to that proposal would assist in its consideration of

the issues presented. Because the alternative proposal stems from the arguments made in Staff’s

Exceptions, the Commission finds no reason to limit the scope of the response to the alternative

compliance proposal. Accordingly, the Commission will permit responses to the Exceptions.

        6.      As the Commission is opening the opportunity to respond for SPS, in the interest

of fairness and equal treatment among the parties, the opportunity to respond shall be available to

all parties, not solely to SPS.

        7.      In response to Staff’s Motion for Oral Argument, the Commission finds that a

formal response from SPS is necessary to fully understand the parties’ respective positions before

ruling on the request.

        8.      Due to the approaching end of the current suspension period on November 30,

2026, the Commission shortens the deadline for filing responses to Exceptions than what SPS had

requested.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

        A.      SPS shall and other parties may file a response to Staff’s Exception by Tuesday,

November 10, 2026. SPS’s response should specifically address Staff’s alternative compliance

filing proposal.

        B.      SPS shall and other parties may file a formal response to Staff’s Motion for Oral

Argument by Tuesday, November 10, 2026.
